summary: Sign in is a passwordless sign-in card in three steps: the person enters an email, types the one-time code they were sent into separate digit boxes, and sees a short confirmation. The code checks itself as soon as the last box is filled. It suits agent products that sign people in by email instead of with a password.
use: When people sign in with an emailed one-time code instead of a password
When the code should be checked the moment it is complete, with no extra submit button
When a wrong code should clear the boxes and let the person try again in place
When you want a resend countdown so people don't request codes over and over
features: The email step checks the address shape and shows `emptyEmailLabel` or `badEmailLabel`, with the field shaking on each failed try.
If `onSendCode` returns a promise, the button spins until it settles, and a rejection's message shows under the field.
The code boxes accept typing, Backspace back to the previous box, and a pasted or autofilled code that spreads across the boxes.

Pass `inbox` and the email with the code arrives at the top of the code screen, the way a phone shows it, with Copy code. Copy puts the code on the clipboard and calls `onCopyCode`; pasting it into the boxes fills them all.
Once every box is filled, `onVerify` runs; returning false clears the boxes and shows `wrongCodeLabel`.
A resend countdown runs from `resendIn` seconds, 30 by default, then turns into a Resend code button that calls `onResend`.
A confirmed code shows a check, then the done screen with `doneTitle`, kept at the height the code screen had, and calls `onSignedIn`.
a11y: Each code box has an `aria-label` like "Digit 1" inside a `group` labelled "Code", and the first box uses `autocomplete="one-time-code"`.
The email input sets `aria-invalid` when the address is missing or malformed.
The resend line is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so verifying, confirmed and wrong code messages are announced.

faq.q: How do I check the code against my backend?
faq.a: Pass `onVerify(code, email)`. Return true, nothing, or a promise of either to accept it. Return false, or throw, and the boxes clear with the wrong code message.

faq.q: Will a one-time code from the phone's keyboard fill all six boxes?
faq.a: The first box has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, and several digits entered at once spread across the boxes from there. Pasting a code into any box fills from the first box.

faq.q: Can I use a four-digit code instead of six?
faq.a: Yes. Set `codeLength` to 4. The default subtitle updates to say how many digits to enter.
